citation: Nunoo, F., Poss, S., Bannermann, P. & Russell, B. 2015. Scorpaena scrofa. The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species 2015: e.T198748A15592127. Accessed on 15 May 2026.

documentation.range: In the eastern Atlantic, this species ranges from the British Isles south to Senegal, including the Cape Verde Islands. It is also found off Angola and off South Africa to Somalia. Identity of materials between Senegal and Angola require confirmation. In the Mediterranean Sea, this species is widely distributed. Records include Iberian coast (Macpherson et al. 2002, Valle et al. 2003), Balearic Sea (Deudero et al. 2004, Moranta et al. 2006, Deudero et al. 2007), Gulf of Lion (Claudet et al. 2006), Ligurian Sea (Molinari and Tunesi 2003, Tunesi and Molinari 2005, Tunesi et al. 2006), Tyrrhenian Sea (La Mesa and Vacchi 1999), Adriatic Sea (Bussotti et al. 2002), Aegean Sea (Moutopoulos and Stergiou 2002, Ayaz et al.2006, Karakulak et al. 2006, Gokce and Metin 2007, Ozaydin et al. 2007) and all other Greek seas (Papaconstantinou 1988). It has a depth distribution of zero to 500 m (Blanc and Hureau 1973).
documentation.population:
In the Eastern Central Atlantic, this species is common and occasionally locally abundant. 

According to Gokce and Metin (2007), seven specimens were collected using three artisanal fishing boats (6.7 and 10 m long) comprising 39 fishing operations. The trials took place between May and October 2003 in Izmir Bay, Turkey. The fishing gear was combined trammel net to trammel net with one lower and one upper part. Each part is formed of three layers: the inner layer with a small mesh size (40 mm stretched mesh), the outer layers with a larger mesh size (220 mm stretched mesh). These nets, each 100 m long and 1.30 m deep, are hung to a common float line and lead line.

Ozaydin et al. (2007) mentioned that 12 specimens were collected from Izmir Bay (central Aegean Sea) between February and December 2005 using bottom trawls (mesh size 24 mm at stretched cod-end), with TL ranging from 10.5 and 28.3 cm.

Karakulak et al. (2006) reported that 15 specimens (12.3 to 39.1 cm TL) were collected from a survey conducted for selectivity by gill and trammel nets in the coastal waters of Turkey from March 2004 to February 2005.

According to Valle et al. (2003), 23 specimens (7.2 to 29.4 cm TL) were collected in November 1995 at six sites along the east coast of Spain (Tabarca, Santa Pola, Postiguet, San Juan, Campello and Villajoyosa). One hundred and eight samples were taken up to a 20-22 m depth, with an approximated duration of 10 min by means of a beam trawl of 1.8 m width and 0.8 m height.

Moutopoulos and Stergiou (2002) mentioned that 37 specimens were collected seasonally during experimental fishing trials conducted with gill nets and long-lines during 1997-98 in the Aegean Sea (Cyclades, coastal waters off Naxos Island, Greece).
documentation.habitats: This is a demersal, non-migratory, solitary and sedentary species that lives over rocky, sandy or muddy substrata. In the Mediterranean Sea, it is often associated with Posidonia oceanica meadows (Moranta et al. 2006, Deudero et al. 2007). It feeds on fishes, crustaceans and molluscs (Hureau and Litvinenko 1986).
documentation.threats: In the Eastern Central Atlantic it is caught primarily as incidental catch but this is not believed to be a major threat. In the Mediterranean, this is a commercial species and its main catching method are trawls, gill nets, trammel nets and long-lines.
documentation.measures: No specific conservation measures are in place for this species.
documentation.use_trade: This species is not sought after for food or trade in west Africa. However, it is occasionally consumed. In the Mediterranean, this is a commercial species.
documentation.rationale: This species has a wide distribution. It is occasionally consumed but it is not removed at any threatening level, and is not believed to have any other major threats affecting it. It is listed as Least Concern with a need for monitoring and more data concerning the disparity of possible ranges, population trend and consumption level.
